answer: Sybil cost is a shared slot: each agent identity must occupy a distinct ledge seat backed by collateral, so cloning keys splits one bond instead of minting free identities. Two conditions hold it. First, registration burns a scarce pulse-window on the public wharf: one hardware pulse, one ledge seat, duplicates slashed at settlement. Second, wharf notaries sample random pulse windows; a key silent through its window forfeits that ledge to the queue. Cloning pays twice for one machine.
